```
Manage teams and team membership.

Teams provide hierarchical grouping of users and workspaces. Teams can be
nested up to 3 levels deep (e.g., /engineering/backend/api).

Usage:
  spin team [flags]
  spin team [command]

Available Commands:
  create      Create a new team
  delete      Delete a team
  get         Get team details
  list        List teams
  member      Manage team members

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for team

Global Flags:
      --config string    config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string    text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")

Use "spin team [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### spin team create

```
Create a new team. Use --parent to nest under an existing team.

Examples:
  spin team create engineering
  spin team create backend --parent engineering
  spin team create api --parent /engineering/backend

Usage:
  spin team create <name> [flags]

Flags:
      --description string   Team description
  -h, --help                 help for create
      --parent string        Parent team ID or path
      --slug string          URL-friendly slug (auto-generated if empty)

Global Flags:
      --config string    config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string    text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")
```

### spin team delete

```
Delete a team. Only team owners can delete teams.
Teams with children cannot be deleted unless --recursive is used.

Usage:
  spin team delete <team-id> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help        help for delete
      --recursive   Delete children too (dangerous!)
  -y, --yes         Skip confirmation

Global Flags:
      --config string    config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string    text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")
```
